CRITICAL TASK — RECOVER, NORMALIZE, AND SECURE THE COMPLETE IVX SOURCE CODE IN OWNER-CONTROLLED GITHUB

PRIORITY: P0 — EXECUTE NOW

CURRENT VERIFIED RISK

The latest audit reports:

- The live backend and Expo application exist inside the Rork workspace.
- Production services are currently running.
- The current GitHub repository does not contain the complete usable source tree.
- The repository contains a broken submodule or pointer structure.
- A clean git clone does not reproduce the working project.
- Important backend, Expo, documentation, Kotlin, and iOS files may exist only inside the workspace.
- If the workspace is deleted, the project could be lost.

This is an existential source-control risk.

Do not start new features.
Do not create more audit narratives.
Do not overwrite or delete the workspace.
Do not reset Git history until a complete backup exists.

==================================================
PRIMARY OBJECTIVE
==================================================

Recover every real IVX source file from the active workspace and create a clean, complete, owner-controlled GitHub repository that:

1. Contains all real source code.
2. Can be cloned normally.
3. Has no broken submodules.
4. Has no dependency on Rork history files.
5. Can install dependencies.
6. Can run tests.
7. Can build the Expo application.
8. Can start the backend.
9. Can deploy to Render.
10. Can rebuild the Android APK.
11. Can be operated without the Rork workspace.

==================================================
PHASE 1 — FREEZE AND BACK UP THE WORKSPACE
==================================================

Before modifying Git:

1. Stop nonessential autonomous file mutations.
2. Record the current production state:
   - GitHub remote URL
   - current branch
   - current local SHA
   - GitHub remote SHA
   - Render deployed SHA
   - runtime health SHA
   - Expo version
   - Android versionCode
   - deployment ID
   - timestamp
3. Create a complete workspace backup.
4. Produce a SHA-256 checksum for the backup.
5. Store the backup in at least two owner-controlled locations:
   - owner-controlled GitHub recovery branch or release asset
   - owner-controlled S3 or equivalent private storage
6. Do not include:
   - node_modules
   - build caches
   - temporary files
   - plaintext secrets
7. Include:
   - backend
   - Expo application
   - all package files
   - lockfiles
   - database migrations
   - scripts
   - tests
   - CI workflows
   - documentation
   - Android native files
   - preserved Kotlin project
   - iOS project directories
   - configuration templates
   - infrastructure files
   - deployment scripts

Return:

- backup filename
- backup size
- backup SHA-256
- file count
- storage locations
- timestamp

Do not continue until the backup is verified readable.

==================================================
PHASE 2 — INVENTORY THE REAL PROJECT
==================================================

Generate a complete source inventory from the active workspace.

Required categories:

1. Backend TypeScript files
2. Backend service modules
3. API route handlers
4. Backend tests
5. Expo screens
6. Expo components
7. Expo library modules
8. Expo tests
9. Android native files
10. Kotlin files
11. iOS project files
12. Database migrations
13. Supabase functions
14. GitHub Actions workflows
15. Render configuration
16. Deployment scripts
17. Documentation
18. Environment-variable templates
19. Autonomous-worker files
20. IVX IA files

For each category return:

- directory
- number of files
- total size
- whether it exists in GitHub
- whether it exists only in the workspace
- whether it is generated
- whether it must be migrated

Create:

- `recovery/workspace-file-inventory.json`
- `recovery/workspace-file-inventory.md`

==================================================
PHASE 3 — IDENTIFY THE BROKEN GIT STRUCTURE
==================================================

Inspect the existing Git repository.

Check:

- `.gitmodules`
- gitlink entries with mode `160000`
- nested `.git` directories
- submodule pointers
- worktrees
- sparse checkout
- LFS pointers
- ignored source directories
- orphaned branches
- untracked files
- files excluded by `.gitignore`
- Rork snapshot commits
- session-summary files
- generated-history files
- commit-tree integrity

Run and save the output of:

- git status
- git remote -v
- git branch -a
- git rev-parse HEAD
- git ls-tree -r HEAD
- git submodule status
- git fsck --full
- git count-objects -vH
- git lfs status, if applicable

Determine exactly why a normal clone returns an unusable project.

Create:

- `recovery/git-root-cause-report.md`

The report must identify:

- broken entry
- affected path
- object type
- expected content
- current content
- recovery method

==================================================
PHASE 4 — CREATE A CLEAN OWNER-CONTROLLED REPOSITORY
==================================================

Do not attempt to preserve a broken tree as the primary repository.

Create or repair one owner-controlled repository as the canonical source of truth.

Required structure:

/
  backend/
  expo/
  android/               if required by the active Expo workflow
  ios/                   only real developed project files
  kotlin-phase-2/        preserved and clearly separated
  supabase/
  scripts/
  tests/
  docs/
  recovery/
  .github/workflows/
  package.json
  lockfile
  README.md
  .gitignore
  .env.example

Rules:

1. Copy actual source files from the working workspace.
2. Do not copy `node_modules`.
3. Do not copy `.git` directories from nested projects.
4. Remove broken gitlinks and submodule pointers.
5. Do not include secrets.
6. Preserve file permissions for executable scripts.
7. Preserve case-sensitive filenames.
8. Preserve all real tests and migrations.
9. Keep Kotlin Phase 2 isolated and unchanged.
10. Do not represent empty iOS scaffolds as complete products.

If the existing repository can be repaired safely, repair it.
If it cannot, create a clean recovery branch or new canonical repository and document the migration.

==================================================
PHASE 5 — SECRET AND CREDENTIAL SAFETY
==================================================

Before committing:

1. Scan the entire recovered tree for:
   - GitHub tokens
   - Render API keys
   - Supabase service-role keys
   - AWS keys
   - JWT secrets
   - passwords
   - private certificates
   - `.env` files
2. Remove all plaintext secrets from source control.
3. Replace them with environment-variable references.
4. Create `.env.example` with variable names only.
5. Rotate credentials that were previously exposed or Rork-managed.
6. Bind replacement credentials only in owner-controlled environments.
7. Run a secret scanner before push.
8. Save a redacted report.

Never print secret values.

==================================================
PHASE 6 — COMMIT THE COMPLETE SOURCE
==================================================

Create commits in a controlled sequence:

Commit 1:
`recovery: add complete IVX workspace source inventory`

Commit 2:
`recovery: restore backend source and tests`

Commit 3:
`recovery: restore Expo application source and tests`

Commit 4:
`recovery: restore infrastructure, migrations, CI, and documentation`

Commit 5:
`recovery: remove broken submodules and normalize repository structure`

Commit 6:
`security: remove secrets and add environment templates`

Commit 7:
`ci: add clean-clone verification workflow`

Push all commits to the owner-controlled repository.

Return:

- repository URL
- branch
- each commit SHA
- final remote SHA
- total tracked files
- total repository size

==================================================
PHASE 7 — CLEAN-CLONE INDEPENDENCE TEST
==================================================

This phase is mandatory.

Use a new empty directory or clean CI runner.

1. Clone the owner-controlled repository.
2. Do not reference the Rork workspace.
3. Confirm no submodule is required.
4. Install dependencies from the committed lockfile.
5. Run TypeScript.
6. Run lint.
7. Run backend tests.
8. Run Expo tests.
9. Run integration tests.
10. Start the backend.
11. Call `/health`.
12. Build the Expo web target if used.
13. Build the Android release artifact.
14. Verify the generated artifact contains the current source SHA.

Record:

- clone command result
- install result
- test totals
- build result
- runtime SHA
- artifact SHA-256
- timestamps

The project is not recovered until a clean clone succeeds.

==================================================
PHASE 8 — RESTORE CI/CD FROM GITHUB
==================================================

Configure GitHub Actions from the owner-controlled repository.

Required workflows:

1. Source integrity
2. Secret scanning
3. TypeScript
4. Lint
5. Backend tests
6. Expo tests
7. Android build
8. Deployment verification
9. Repository clean-clone proof

Render must deploy from the correct owner-controlled repository and branch.

Verify:

- Render repository binding
- branch binding
- auto-deploy policy
- build command
- start command
- environment variables
- deployed commit SHA
- runtime health SHA

Require:

GitHub HEAD SHA
=
Render deployed SHA
=
runtime `/health` SHA

==================================================
PHASE 9 — REBUILD THE CURRENT APK
==================================================

Build a new Android release from the recovered repository.

Requirements:

- source: clean owner-controlled GitHub clone
- version incremented
- versionCode incremented
- signed release artifact
- no debug keystore for production distribution
- APK SHA-256 recorded
- source commit embedded or reported
- direct persistent download location
- GitHub Release asset preferred
- installation test completed
- launch test completed
- owner login tested

Return:

- filename
- version
- versionCode
- source SHA
- APK SHA-256
- permanent download location
- installation result
- launch result

==================================================
PHASE 10 — REAL DEVICE QA
==================================================

After repository recovery, test the rebuilt APK on at least one real Android device.

Test:

1. Installation
2. Launch
3. Owner login
4. Logout
5. Session persistence
6. App restart
7. Home feed
8. Investment Cards
9. Reels
10. View Deal
11. Invest Now
12. Registration
13. Waitlist
14. Messages
15. Notifications
16. Image upload
17. Video upload
18. PDF upload
19. Search
20. Settings
21. Owner controls
22. Network interruption and recovery
23. No crash
24. No page jumping
25. No infinite loading

For each test record:

- device model
- Android version
- app version
- test timestamp
- result
- screenshot or log
- trace ID when applicable

Do not report file-existence checks as device QA.

==================================================
PHASE 11 — BACKEND TEST COVERAGE
==================================================

The audit reports that many services and handlers have no dedicated tests.

Create a coverage map:

- service file
- route handler
- existing test
- missing test
- risk
- priority

Do not claim the backend is fully tested because existing tests pass.

Prioritize tests for:

1. Authentication
2. Owner-only authorization
3. Members
4. Investors
5. Buyers
6. Deals
7. Payments
8. Uploads
9. Messages
10. Notifications
11. Autonomous jobs
12. GitHub execution
13. Render deployment
14. Database mutations
15. Retry and rollback behavior

Target for this recovery phase:

- 100% of critical routes covered
- 100% of owner/security routes covered
- all currently failing tests fixed
- no fake passing tests
- no skipped critical tests

==================================================
PHASE 12 — AUTONOMOUS 24/7 RECOVERY TRACKING
==================================================

IVX Autonomous must track this recovery as persistent tasks.

Required task states:

- QUEUED
- RUNNING
- BACKING_UP
- INVENTORYING
- MIGRATING
- TESTING
- PUSHING
- DEPLOYING
- VERIFYING
- VERIFIED
- RETRYING
- BLOCKED
- FAILED

Create a parent recovery job and child tasks for every phase.

Every two hours, IVX IA Chat must post:

IVX SOURCE RECOVERY — 2-HOUR REPORT

- Report timestamp
- Parent job ID
- Active phase
- Active task
- Worker heartbeat
- Files backed up
- Files migrated
- Git commits created
- GitHub remote SHA
- Tests passed
- Tests failed
- Deployment status
- APK status
- Real-device QA status
- Current blockers
- Automatic recovery attempts
- Next two-hour plan
- Overall recovery percentage

Reports must be generated from real persisted job data.

==================================================
FINAL ACCEPTANCE PROOF
==================================================

Return one final evidence package containing:

1. Workspace backup location and SHA-256
2. Full workspace file inventory
3. Git root-cause report
4. Canonical owner-controlled GitHub repository
5. Clean repository tree
6. Final GitHub SHA
7. Clean-clone logs
8. Dependency-install logs
9. TypeScript result
10. Lint result
11. Backend-test result
12. Expo-test result
13. Integration-test result
14. GitHub Actions results
15. Render deployment ID
16. Render deployed SHA
17. Runtime health SHA
18. APK filename and SHA-256
19. Persistent APK download location
20. Real-device QA matrix
21. Secret-scan report
22. Credential-rotation report
23. Remaining untested-service map
24. Remaining risks
25. Overall verified percentage

==================================================
SUCCESS CONDITION
==================================================

Do not mark this task complete merely because files were pushed.

This recovery is complete only when:

- The complete working source exists in owner-controlled GitHub.
- A fresh clone contains the complete project.
- No broken gitlink or submodule remains.
- The backend builds and tests from the fresh clone.
- The Expo app builds and tests from the fresh clone.
- Render deploys from the recovered repository.
- GitHub, Render, and runtime SHAs match.
- A new APK is built from the recovered SHA.
- The APK installs and runs on a real Android device.
- Secrets are removed and rotated.
- The Rork workspace is no longer the only copy of the code.
- IVX can continue development independently of Rork.

START NOW WITH PHASE 1:
FREEZE MUTATIONS, BACK UP THE ENTIRE WORKSPACE, CALCULATE THE BACKUP SHA-256, AND VERIFY THE BACKUP BEFORE CHANGING GIT.
